subject: Retaillytics — econ probes & caching/batching matrix (post-demo)
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@retaillytics.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.example, ben.carter@redwood.example
Date: 2028-11-20T16:12:00-08:00
Subject: Retaillytics / Redwood demo — next econ probes

Rafael / Ben,

Thanks again for walking the team through the demo today — appreciate the focus on predictable latency and the routing/fallback options. A few quick takeaways from our side and the things Procurement & Engineering asked us to nail down before we can move forward: 

- Economics comparison: we need a per-1M tokens cost comparison for the model variants you showed vs the hyperscaler endpoints our infra team is evaluating (AWS Bedrock + Llama family, and GCP Vertex). Please show both cold/no-cache and with a prefix/KV-cache hit rate sensitivity (10%, 50%, 90%).
- Batching sensitivity: show effective per-token cost at batching sizes 1, 8, 32, 128 for the same traffic profile.
- Production probe: Engineering wants a short canary-style run (100k tokens) using a mix of representative prompts from our product (I can attach a sample set). Please include end-to-end latency percentiles and token-ops breakdown (model compute vs I/O).
- Procurement asks: SOC2 evidence + standard SOW template and a sample pricing calc sheet we can drop into our procurement system.

Attaching the recording for your reference. Would like a proposed plan and timeline by Wednesday EOD if possible so we can align internal stakeholders.

Alex
Director of AI Product
Retaillytics

--
Attachment: demo-recording.mp4 (video/mp4, 42MB stub)

From: rafael.mendes@redwood.example
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@retaillytics.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.example, laura.bennett@redwood.example
Date: 2028-11-21T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Retaillytics / Redwood demo — next econ probes

Alex — great to hear; glad the demo was useful. Below is a concise plan and the assumptions we'll use for the comparative worksheet and probe runs. We'll start as soon as you confirm the sample prompts and procurement contact.

Plan (high level):
1) Comparative worksheet (deliverable: redwood-econ-snapshot.xlsx)
   - Compare per-1M token economics for 3 endpoints: Redwood-hosted (production model variant), AWS Bedrock (model X.x), GCP Vertex (model Y.y).
   - Assumptions: avg sequence length (prompt+response) = 120 tokens; temperature/decoding cost normalized; memory/kv-cache savings applied on hit rates.
   - Sensitivity slices: cache hit = 0%, 10%, 50%, 90%; batching = 1, 8, 32, 128. Output: per-1M tokens cost + 95th pctl latency uplift.

2) Microbench matrix (deliverable: proposed-test-matrix.csv + run artifacts)
   - We will run a matrix of 12 micro-runs that cross batching x cache-hit assumptions using our dedicated test harness. We'll simulate network latency similar to your prod region (us-west-2) and report p50/p90/p99 and token-op breakdown. Run artifacts will be uploaded to s3 (link below).

3) Canary probe (deliverable: short-run report + traces)
   - 100k tokens across the sample prompt set you provide. We'll run 3 iterations staggered across times of day to surface cache-warmup effects and variance.

Timeline: 7 business days from receipt of sample prompts + procurement contact.

Immediate asks for us to start:
- Sample prompt file (CSV or JSONL)
- Procurement contact (email) for SOC2 and SOW routing

I've attached the initial econ snapshot with placeholder numbers and the proposed matrix schema. Ben & Laura, can you review assumptions on token length and pricing inputs (I used conservative q1 pricing for hosted unit ops)?

Thanks — will hold a 30m readout slot once we have results.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-econ-snapshot.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), proposed-test-matrix.csv (text/csv)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.example>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.example, rafael.mendes@redwood.example
Date: 2028-11-21T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Retaillytics / Redwood demo — quick internal notes

Quick internal note — forwarding for visibility. A couple of practical assumptions I recommend we lock before the runs: 

- Token assumptions: use 120 tokens average as Rafa suggested but also produce a 60/120/300 token column so they can see short/median/long behavior.
- Pricing inputs (example for snapshot):
    * Redwood hosted baseline: $0.00055 per input token compute-equivalent (pre-cache) — include line items for batching delta and kv-cache savings
    * Bedrock / Vertex: use published MSRP + add 10% for egress/infra delta where appropriate
- Cache model: simulate cheap prefix caching (only first prompt token vectorized) and KV cache hit (full window reuse). Show both as separate series.

I'll prepare a short note on how we simulate p99 tails under burst. Laura — can you confirm we're comfortable with the proposed run matrix and whether we want to include quantized runtime variants?

Ben
Head of Benchmarking

Rafael — thanks, that plan looks good. Two quick items attached below:

- sample-prompts.jsonl (100 rows with short/med/long examples)
- procurement contact: Mary Lin <mary.lin@retaillytics.com> (procurement lead)

Procurement also asked for a simple SOW template and a SOC2 link (we can accept your hosted SOC2 report). Mary is the primary contact for legal and procurement approvals.

Accepted timeline: 7 business days works for us. Please schedule a 30-minute results review; I'm available Friday 10:00–12:00 PST or Monday 14:00–17:00 PST.

One more ask for the deliverable: include a short-run comparison that shows the marginal unit cost improvement when moving from batching=1 to batching=8 and when cache hit increases from 10% to 50% — that delta is what our CFO cares about.

Thanks again; looking forward to the snapshot.

Alex
Director of AI Product
Retaillytics
